faq.a: Gavrilo Princip, a 19-year-old Bosnian Serb who wanted Bosnia freed from Austria-Hungary. He shot the Archduke and his wife Sophie in Sarajevo on 28 June 1914.
The assassins had been armed and helped by a secret Serbian nationalist group, the Black Hand. Austria-Hungary sent Serbia harsh demands, and declared war on 28 July 1914 when not all were accepted.

faq.q: Why did Britain join the war?
faq.a: Britain had promised in an 1839 treaty to protect Belgium's neutrality, and it feared German power in Europe. When Germany invaded Belgium, Britain declared war on 4 August 1914.
asks: Why did Britain declare war on Germany?

faq.q: What were the alliances before World War One?
faq.a: The Triple Entente of France, Russia and Britain, and the Triple Alliance of Germany, Austria-Hungary and Italy. Italy later switched sides and joined the Allies in 1915.
asks: What were the two sides in World War One?

faq.a: Militarism, Alliances, Imperialism and Nationalism: four long-term causes of the First World War. Historians still debate which mattered most and how much blame each country deserves.
asks: What were the main causes of World War One?

facts: Archduke Franz Ferdinand was assassinated in Sarajevo on 28 June 1914.
Britain declared war on Germany on 4 August 1914.
About 65 million people were mobilised to fight in the First World War.
